newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Late Western Cape rains worry S.African farmers.
newsitem.headline: Late Western Cape rains worry S.African farmers.

text.p: Unseasonal, heavy late rains are causing concern among farmers in South Africa's Western Cape province as they try to harvest winter grain.
Wheat and barley farmers, who started harvesting in October, report that the rains had forced them to halt their machines and wait for the ground to dry out.
The rains were expected to lower yields of crops still in the ground but the full effect of this could not yet be determined, they said.
But KWV extension services manager Jan Booysen told Reuters on Friday that rain was welcome for farmers who did not have irrigation.
University of Stellenbosch horticulture professor Gerard Jacobs said fruit growers were also having problems controlling fungus diseases.

Many fruit trees had already budded and the young fruit was vulnerable, he said, adding that it was too early to judge the effect this might have on the harvest. --Lynda Loxton, Cape Town newsroom +27 21 25-2238
